name: Rhenium

discovery.discoverer: Walter Noddack, Ida Noddack & Otto Berg

occurrence: One of the rarest elements in Earth's crust, found only in trace amounts within molybdenum ores.
majorUses: Jet engine turbine blade superalloys (extreme heat resistance)
Catalysts for high-octane, lead-free gasoline production
Electrical contacts and thermocouples for very high temperatures
notableCharacteristics: One of the last stable elements to be discovered (1925), named after the Rhine river.
ncertRelevance: among the last stable elements discovered
whyHere: Its half-filled-adjacent 5d⁵ configuration gives rhenium exceptional strength and one of the highest melting points of any element, exactly the property that makes it indispensable in the hottest-running parts of jet engines.
didYouKnow: Jet engine turbine blades routinely contain a few percent rhenium specifically because it lets the blades survive temperatures otherwise close to melting the metal itself.
genZNote: One of the last stable elements ever found, and now it's the reason jet engines don't melt mid-flight. No pressure.
